top.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
top.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. top.title: Astronomers watch a red giant star greedily devour a stellar 'Bao bun' before erupting: 'We couldn't quite believe our luck'
top.description: null Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER). "The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events." Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy , a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion. Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years, They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. They linked this to a star called WNTR23bzdiq / WTP19aalzlk that had been observed steadily brightening since 2019 after being stable for the preceding 30 years. Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. The team theorizes that Big Bao, with a mass seven times greater than the sun, expanded so rapidly and violently that it swallowed its smaller companion star. The unfortunate star, Little Bao, then spiraled into Big Bao's core in fewer than 10 orbits. "A couple of years back, we discovered a star that was gradually brightening. We took a closer look to discover a red giant, or a star that has started to expand toward the end of its life, just like our sun will one day," Karambelkar said. "Steady brightening was unusual, but even if something was stirring, no one expected to see an explosion in their lifetime, as these stars remain relatively stable for thousands of years." The Portuguese manager addressed the growing hype during Friday's press conference, offering a measured verdict on how the two midfield greats should be viewed. Mourinho shuts down Zidane comparisons Mourinho has distanced himself from the growing debate linking Bellingham to Zidane. The comparisons surfaced earlier this week after the England midfielder delivered a standout display in Europe. Bellingham drew widespread acclaim following Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League triumph over PSV. His commanding performance prompted observers to draw parallels with the legendary French playmaker. However, when asked about the link during his media duties on Friday, Mourinho made it clear he has no interest in pitting the two players against each other. Different eras, same elite status Rather than weighing one midfielder's qualities against the other, the Portuguese tactician stressed that both players deserve to be judged strictly within their own eras. Mourinho believes generational gaps make direct comparisons pointless. "I don't like comparing footballers from different generations," Mourinho told reporters on Friday. "Zidane was one of the best of his generation and Jude is already one of the best of his." Bellingham's impressive numbers and humble view The praise surrounding Bellingham has been fuelled by his consistent output throughout the current campaign. At just 23 years old, the midfielder has already registered seven goals in 18 appearances across all competitions for Madrid this season. His display in the five-goal rout of PSV only intensified the spotlight. Yet despite his rapid rise and growing influence in Madrid, the England international remains grounded about his place in football history. When previously confronted with the same comparisons, Bellingham himself played down the hype , insisting that Zidane was "much better" than him. top.description: ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany Werder Bremen is the best team in northern Germany. At least that is what was evident from last weekend’s Nordderby, when they successfully beat Hamburg 4–0 at the Weserstadion. Bremen did more than just win that game; they demonstrated their quality this season and their ability to maximise the potential of their players to become a highly efficient team. This is the issue: The underlying numbers, in this case expected goals (xG), indicate that the game was actually very close – not as one-sided as the result suggests. HSV even had 1.54 compared to Bremen’s 1.52 in front of xG, per Opta. So, being able to win by a four-goal margin despite losing on xG shows just how effective Bremen are as a team. Get German Football News’ Bergas investigates why… First thing first: Underlying numbers need context Yes, HSV has more numbers in front of xG. However, if we look at the xG data itself, 1.03 of HSV’s 1.54 came after they fell behind in the 55th minute. In this situation, the state of the game changed, with HSV adopting a more proactive approach with the ball. Meanwhile, between minutes 1 and 54, when the score was still 0–0, HSV only achieved an xG of 0.5 (Bremen had 0.84). This is why xG is not the best metric with which to measure HSV’s performance in this game, because the state of the game forced them to create more chances in order to catch up, resulting in lots of shots. In fact, however, they weren’t really dangerous enough to challenge or harm Bremen. Looking at other metrics such as key passes, HSV weren’t superior either during the even time when the score was still 0–0. In that period, they made four key passes compared to Bremen’s eight. HSV found it much harder to create shots than the home team. Even in the first half, when Bremen were underperforming in parts, HSV didn’t look particularly threatening. Bremen flexible defensive structure made HSV toothless One of the reasons for that is Bremen’s flexibility in their approach to HSV when defending. In the first half, they often used a man-to-man approach (which was more aggressive), which successfully forced HSV to use long balls to progress the ball to the final third, particularly on their left side. In this long-ball scenario, Bremen also had the advantage when it came to closing down HSV attacks. The problem for Bremen arose when HSV successfully won the second ball, creating a situation in which Amos Pieper had to defend one-on-one against the opponent. Pieper struggled in the early stages of the game against HSV’s pacey attackers and received a yellow card in the first half, but played safely for the rest of the game and successfully avoided another red card. top.title: Powerful Storm Disrupts US Thanksgiving, Leaves Over 900,000 Without Power
top.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were cancelled, and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organisers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was cancelled for three years during World War II. Organisers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. Stay Safe People brave the bad weather in the Manhattan borough of New York City on November 26, 2026. Photo by KENA BETANCUR / AFP While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes. Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption. Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency Wednesday over the weather, urged residents to take precautions to stay safe. “Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines,” she wrote on X. Some people improvised to still enjoy Thanksgiving, which is traditionally marked by gathering with family around a large meal, with turkey as the centerpiece. “No electricity? No problem,” celebrity chef Jose Andres wrote on X, alongside a video of a candlelit dining room and lobsters cooking on a gas-powered stove. top.title: Eight-time champion Marquez to retire from MotoGP
top.description: Marc Marquez's eight MotoGP titles have come between 2013 and 2026 [Getty Images] MotoGP champion Marc Marquez has said he will retire days after clinching a record-equalling eighth title. The 33-year-old Spaniard clinched the 2026 world championship in Portugal last weekend, putting him level with Giacomo Agostini and one clear of modern great Valentino Rossi. The Ducati rider had extended his contract until 2028 in June but will now end his professional career after the final race of the season in Valencia on Sunday. "Thank you to everyone who's been part of the journey," he said. "I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have." Marquez won his first title in 2013 and remains the only rider to win a MotoGP championship in his rookie year. He began his MotoGP career with Honda, winning six titles in seven seasons up to 2019. After joining Gresini Racing - the satellite Ducati team - for 2024, he spent the past two seasons with the Italian outfit's factory team - winning the championship in both. "It is official," read a team statement. "Marc Marquez has decided to retire from MotoGP, and the 2026 Valencia Grand Prix will be his final race as a professional rider and with the Ducati Lenovo team." top.title: 'That's his problem!' - Vinicius Jr handed blunt reality check by Jose Mourinho as Real Madrid boss demands collective sacrifice ahead of Alaves clash
top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-REAL MADRID-INTER MILAN - AFP Jose Mourinho has sent a clear message to Vinicius Jr and the rest of his Real Madrid stars, insisting that individual reputations mean nothing compared to the needs of the collective. Speaking ahead of the clash with Alaves, the Portuguese coach made it clear that even the biggest names at the Bernabeu must accept their role for the good of the team. Mourinho dismisses guaranteed starting spots The 'Special One' has rejected the idea of a fixed starting line-up at Real Madrid ahead of Saturday night’s La Liga clash against Deportivo Alaves. Addressing the media, the Portuguese coach faced repeated questions over whether Vinicius Jr has done enough to reclaim a regular berth. Mourinho insisted recent speculation around Vinicius’s future and his compatibility with Real's record signing Yan Diomande carries no weight inside the club. While acknowledging the Brazilian has improved, he stressed that team unity always overrides individual standing. 'That's his problem!' Asked how Vinicius compares to Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham - with Bellingham benched only once this season - Mourinho delivered a blunt verdict, attributing their heavy involvement strictly to superior displays. "That’s his problem, not mine," Mourinho said of Vinicius's place in the side. "Mbappe and Bellingham are on the same level as everyone else. If they end up on the bench someday… that’s just how it is. The collective goal is above the individual. The difference lies in their incomparable performance compared to the rest." He also dismissed hints of rivalry between Vinicius and Diomande after their recent celebrations together: "It’s not about competition, we’re all together and we all want the same thing. We’re achieving stability and it seems your objective is to create this doubt. Nobody on the team wants that." Squad depth and unity driving Madrid's resurgence Over his five months in charge, Mourinho has built a steady environment that contrasts with last season’s dressing-room problems. That depth showed when Thibaut Courtois missed his only game through illness, allowing Andriy Lunin to step in and prove decisive. "We have been together for five months and we haven’t had any issues," Mourinho explained. "People want to play; nobody likes being left out or not getting minutes. The collective objective will overcome any individual egos." top.title: Will Stein explains his decision to not call plays for Kentucky Football
top.description: Will Stein’s debut season as a head coach has been a success. The last three games have brought some negativity within the fanbase, but overall, and especially if you can go win the Governor’s Cup to get your eighth win of the season, it’s a successful year one. Stein took over a program with a difficult schedule and not a ton of pieces returning, and entered the year with a betting over/under of 4.5 wins, and got the over on that on October 10 when Kentucky stunned LSU in its second straight victory after beating South Carolina in the same fashion a week earlier. Well, going into the season, there was one decision Stein made that turned some heads and brought some questioning. He said he wouldn’t be calling the offense and that he wants to be a great head coach rather than just an offensive mind. Now, he did mention it’ll have his input, and he won’t abandon it completely, but he would allow the offensive play-calling to be done by former LSU offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. Why is that? Well, Stein answered that with a detailed explanation this week. “I think as a competitor, you want to be in that spot,” Stein said. “But I know for the good of the entire organization, not just the on-the-field play, but recruiting, sports strength and conditioning, our training room, nutrition, fundraising, everything that embodies being a head coach in today’s college football, it was important for me to be at my best for the entirety of the organization. “What we do on Saturdays is really a collection of everybody in our offensive staff room, defensive staff room, special teams room, and using that collaboration and the brain power that we have to formulate the best possible plan that we feel like can go win a football game. And just because I’m not saying it over the mic to the quarterback doesn’t mean that I don’t have my hands in those decisions. “I feel like Joe Sloan has done a fantastic job this season. We’ve battled through ups and downs and adversity. And what I love about Joe is his confidence, his ability to communicate, his ability to connect with players.” Stein then added more on Sloan, saying, “The confidence that he gives our players and our team is really special. And so I’ve been very proud of him and developing this relationship that we have here at Kentucky together.” Stein certainly acknowledged the dip in scoring production in the last three contests after scoring only six against Tennessee, 14 against Florida, and 14 at Missouri, but shows some excitement in the potential of the offense in Saturday’s game against Louisville and onto the postseason. So far, it’s been a success to have Sloan call the plays, with a little bit of Stein’s input during game-planning. Let’s hope this offense can find a way to take care of it, score the ball, and get back to the way it showed earlier in the season.

top.title: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun
top.description: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun Filipe Luís has paid tribute to Folarin Balogun’s (25) attitude since returning from the most recent international break. The USMNT forward netted a brace as AS Monaco beat Hearts in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday night. Paris Brunner missed the game in Scotland due to a muscular injury, so it was a chance for Balogun to re-establish himself at Monaco. The former Arsenal man missed the start of the season due to injury and his summer was also marked by the episode of his failed move to Everton. Since returning to fitness, Balogun has failed to replicate the kind of form that saw him become the subject of a €50m approach from Everton. Speaking last week, Filipe Luís evoked the American’s situation: “ For me, it’s very simple. Monaco is bigger than any player. It’s bigger than everybody. And I want players who want to be here, of course. And I need Balogun to feel that he belongs here, that he wants to play here, because then if he plays, he scores goals; it’s going to be easier to make him fulfil his objective .” Just days before, Balogun had reaffirmed his ambition to leave Monaco in the near future. Luís has now praised the forward, who he says has returned from this month’s international break “with a different attitude.” ”He had a summer that was difficult to come to terms with , like Lamine Camara, who was also close to leaving. It is difficult to experience, especially after having played in the World Cup and having heard so many rumours in the press. That also explains why he found it difficult to come back. “Since he came back in November, he has really come back with a different attitude. He is a super player who could still leave in January but until then, he is still a Monaco player and I hope that I will still be able to benefit from him,” said Luís after his brace in the win over Hearts (2-3). top.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
top.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. top.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
top.description: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The six-week exercise will give players and support staff who were part of the tour an opportunity to share their experiences, although individual accounts will remain confidential and will not be made available to the CA Board. The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations. The document will not include individual testimonies or any supporting material. CA has also committed to releasing the complete report, together with its response, within 30 days of receiving it. The independent exercise will be overseen by senior counsel Fiona McLeod AO SC, who will conduct private sessions with those willing to participate. The forum was announced following fresh revelations surrounding the 2018 scandal in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr . In the book, Khawaja claimed that awareness of the sandpaper plan extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned by CA. David Warner and Cameron Bancroft have supported parts of his account, while Pat Cummins and several other bowlers have maintained that they had no knowledge of the plan. The forum will examine Australia's ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season, the team's involvement in all four Tests of the South Africa tour, and the incident involving Bancroft during the third Test in Cape Town on March 24, 2018. It will also look into CA's subsequent investigation into the episode. However, the exercise is not intended to reopen the original investigation or establish individual responsibility for the incident. CA has extended invitations to all players and support staff who were part of the South Africa tour, along with the management officials and board directors who were associated with the organisation at the time. Participants will be able to share their accounts through face-to-face or online meetings with McLeod, submit written statements or provide relevant documents. Taking part in the process is voluntary, and those who choose to participate will be permitted to have a support person or legal representative present. The terms of reference also lay down safeguards to protect the confidentiality of participants. Information shared by one individual cannot be attributed to them when seeking clarification from another participant unless they provide consent. Those involved will be informed about who can access their submissions and will have the opportunity to verify their own accounts for accuracy. In addition, the forum will be given access to the 2018 Culture and Governance Review of Australian Cricket conducted by The Ethics Centre, along with other relevant records and documents it considers necessary. top.title: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.”
top.description: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.” The strength of Hoffenheim’s bench proved decisive in Thursday evening’s 3-1 Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz. Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club. Hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him. “No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.” Hoffenheim’s substitutes deliver decisive contributions Ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker. Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench. “Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.” Hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen , Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist. Despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half. Baumann acknowledged that Hoffenheim remain in a developmental phase. nigeria.title: Powerful Storm Disrupts US Thanksgiving, Leaves Over 900,000 Without Power
nigeria.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were cancelled, and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organisers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was cancelled for three years during World War II. Organisers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. Stay Safe People brave the bad weather in the Manhattan borough of New York City on November 26, 2026. Photo by KENA BETANCUR / AFP While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes. Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption. Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency Wednesday over the weather, urged residents to take precautions to stay safe. “Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines,” she wrote on X. Some people improvised to still enjoy Thanksgiving, which is traditionally marked by gathering with family around a large meal, with turkey as the centerpiece. “No electricity? While armed conflict and violence are the main reasons for acute food insecurity around the globe, dramatic climate events, including El Nino, are another driver, the joint report from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP) said. The Rome-based agencies listed Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen as the areas of highest concern in its early warning about 16 “hunger hotspots” from December until May 2027. Famine remains a “plausible” risk in parts of Sudan — including North Darfur — and South Sudan, the report found. ‘Alarming levels of displacement’ The indoor cooking setup of a local food vendor, featuring large metal pots resting on industrial gas stoves. nigeria.title: Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Singer-songwriter and record producer Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has said the “rig and die” slogan sounds correct as a response to election rigging, but warned that innocent people must not be caught up in the resulting violence. He spoke in an interview on Nigeria Info’s WhatsUpLagos show while responding to the slogan ahead of the 2027 elections. The ace singer said frustration over impunity had made calls for severe punishment understandable, while stressing that allegations of rigging must be proven. “You know when a situation gets to a certain point, like right now we’re like on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make you make some kind of statements. This statement sounds correct. It should be like that, actually.” He said the slogan reflected a demand for stronger consequences for election rigging. “If you rig, the punishments should be very severe to deter people from rigging.” 2Baba added: “So the statement itself is rig or die. You understand what I’m saying? So for me, the statement itself, it shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone by. So for me, I don’t see nothing wrong with that statement.” However, he warned against innocent people being harmed in the name of enforcing the slogan. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this fight because some people might not rig, they might just be there. A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). In this situation, the state of the game changed, with HSV adopting a more proactive approach with the ball. Meanwhile, between minutes 1 and 54, when the score was still 0–0, HSV only achieved an xG of 0.5 (Bremen had 0.84). This is why xG is not the best metric with which to measure HSV’s performance in this game, because the state of the game forced them to create more chances in order to catch up, resulting in lots of shots. He also dismissed hints of rivalry between Vinicius and Diomande after their recent celebrations together: "It’s not about competition, we’re all together and we all want the same thing. We’re achieving stability and it seems your objective is to create this doubt. Nobody on the team wants that." Squad depth and unity driving Madrid's resurgence Over his five months in charge, Mourinho has built a steady environment that contrasts with last season’s dressing-room problems. That depth showed when Thibaut Courtois missed his only game through illness, allowing Andriy Lunin to step in and prove decisive. "We have been together for five months and we haven’t had any issues," Mourinho explained. "People want to play; nobody likes being left out or not getting minutes. The collective objective will overcome any individual egos." Title pressure mounts as transfer stance becomes clear Beating Alaves on Saturday will seal an 11th straight win across all competitions for Los Blancos, who have won every match since the first international break and thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League this week. Victory will also pile pressure on La Liga leaders Barcelona, who sit three points ahead before playing on Sunday. With two months left until the transfer window opens, Mourinho also shut down squad exit or arrival talk: "I don’t want anyone coming in and out. I don’t want any transfer rumours."

sports.title: Argyle's fit-again Oseni making up for lost time
sports.description: Owen Oseni has featured as a substitute in Plymouth's past two League One games [Shutterstock] Plymouth Argyle striker Owen Oseni hopes he can re-establish himself in the side after returning to full fitness. The 23-year-old, who won his first cap for Nigeria over the summer, has recovered from an ankle injury he suffered in late September. "It's all part of the game but I don't think I've ever experienced this side of the game, picking up two injuries in such quick succession. "So it was good to learn, just experience that part of the game and just make sure I stay focused, I do my work in the gym and try to come back as quick as I can to help the lads." Plymouth Argyle striker Oseni suffers injury blow Plymouth target attacking signing after Oseni injury Plymouth striker Oseni makes Nigeria debut Oseni has not started a league game since Argyle's 2-2 draw with Exeter City in April. sports.title: Will Stein explains his decision to not call plays for Kentucky Football
sports.description: Will Stein’s debut season as a head coach has been a success. The last three games have brought some negativity within the fanbase, but overall, and especially if you can go win the Governor’s Cup to get your eighth win of the season, it’s a successful year one. Stein took over a program with a difficult schedule and not a ton of pieces returning, and entered the year with a betting over/under of 4.5 wins, and got the over on that on October 10 when Kentucky stunned LSU in its second straight victory after beating South Carolina in the same fashion a week earlier. Well, going into the season, there was one decision Stein made that turned some heads and brought some questioning. He said he wouldn’t be calling the offense and that he wants to be a great head coach rather than just an offensive mind. Now, he did mention it’ll have his input, and he won’t abandon it completely, but he would allow the offensive play-calling to be done by former LSU offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. Why is that? Well, Stein answered that with a detailed explanation this week. “I think as a competitor, you want to be in that spot,” Stein said. “But I know for the good of the entire organization, not just the on-the-field play, but recruiting, sports strength and conditioning, our training room, nutrition, fundraising, everything that embodies being a head coach in today’s college football, it was important for me to be at my best for the entirety of the organization. “What we do on Saturdays is really a collection of everybody in our offensive staff room, defensive staff room, special teams room, and using that collaboration and the brain power that we have to formulate the best possible plan that we feel like can go win a football game. And just because I’m not saying it over the mic to the quarterback doesn’t mean that I don’t have my hands in those decisions. “I feel like Joe Sloan has done a fantastic job this season. We’ve battled through ups and downs and adversity. And what I love about Joe is his confidence, his ability to communicate, his ability to connect with players.” Stein then added more on Sloan, saying, “The confidence that he gives our players and our team is really special. And so I’ve been very proud of him and developing this relationship that we have here at Kentucky together.” Stein certainly acknowledged the dip in scoring production in the last three contests after scoring only six against Tennessee, 14 against Florida, and 14 at Missouri, but shows some excitement in the potential of the offense in Saturday’s game against Louisville and onto the postseason. So far, it’s been a success to have Sloan call the plays, with a little bit of Stein’s input during game-planning. Let’s hope this offense can find a way to take care of it, score the ball, and get back to the way it showed earlier in the season.

sports.title: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun
sports.description: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun Filipe Luís has paid tribute to Folarin Balogun’s (25) attitude since returning from the most recent international break. The USMNT forward netted a brace as AS Monaco beat Hearts in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday night. Paris Brunner missed the game in Scotland due to a muscular injury, so it was a chance for Balogun to re-establish himself at Monaco. The former Arsenal man missed the start of the season due to injury and his summer was also marked by the episode of his failed move to Everton. Since returning to fitness, Balogun has failed to replicate the kind of form that saw him become the subject of a €50m approach from Everton. Speaking last week, Filipe Luís evoked the American’s situation: “ For me, it’s very simple. Monaco is bigger than any player. It’s bigger than everybody. And I want players who want to be here, of course. And I need Balogun to feel that he belongs here, that he wants to play here, because then if he plays, he scores goals; it’s going to be easier to make him fulfil his objective .” Just days before, Balogun had reaffirmed his ambition to leave Monaco in the near future. Luís has now praised the forward, who he says has returned from this month’s international break “with a different attitude.” ”He had a summer that was difficult to come to terms with , like Lamine Camara, who was also close to leaving. It is difficult to experience, especially after having played in the World Cup and having heard so many rumours in the press. That also explains why he found it difficult to come back. “Since he came back in November, he has really come back with a different attitude. He is a super player who could still leave in January but until then, he is still a Monaco player and I hope that I will still be able to benefit from him,” said Luís after his brace in the win over Hearts (2-3). sports.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
sports.description: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The six-week exercise will give players and support staff who were part of the tour an opportunity to share their experiences, although individual accounts will remain confidential and will not be made available to the CA Board. The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations. The document will not include individual testimonies or any supporting material. CA has also committed to releasing the complete report, together with its response, within 30 days of receiving it. The independent exercise will be overseen by senior counsel Fiona McLeod AO SC, who will conduct private sessions with those willing to participate. The forum was announced following fresh revelations surrounding the 2018 scandal in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr . In the book, Khawaja claimed that awareness of the sandpaper plan extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned by CA. David Warner and Cameron Bancroft have supported parts of his account, while Pat Cummins and several other bowlers have maintained that they had no knowledge of the plan. The forum will examine Australia's ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season, the team's involvement in all four Tests of the South Africa tour, and the incident involving Bancroft during the third Test in Cape Town on March 24, 2018. It will also look into CA's subsequent investigation into the episode. However, the exercise is not intended to reopen the original investigation or establish individual responsibility for the incident. CA has extended invitations to all players and support staff who were part of the South Africa tour, along with the management officials and board directors who were associated with the organisation at the time. Participants will be able to share their accounts through face-to-face or online meetings with McLeod, submit written statements or provide relevant documents. Taking part in the process is voluntary, and those who choose to participate will be permitted to have a support person or legal representative present. The terms of reference also lay down safeguards to protect the confidentiality of participants. Information shared by one individual cannot be attributed to them when seeking clarification from another participant unless they provide consent. Those involved will be informed about who can access their submissions and will have the opportunity to verify their own accounts for accuracy. In addition, the forum will be given access to the 2018 Culture and Governance Review of Australian Cricket conducted by The Ethics Centre, along with other relevant records and documents it considers necessary. sports.title: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.”
sports.description: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.” The strength of Hoffenheim’s bench proved decisive in Thursday evening’s 3-1 Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz. Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club. Hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him. “No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.” Hoffenheim’s substitutes deliver decisive contributions Ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker. Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench. “Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.” Hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen , Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist. Despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half. Baumann acknowledged that Hoffenheim remain in a developmental phase. The German international nevertheless welcomed the response after halftime, which helped lift Ilzer’s side to 15th place in the Europa League standings. Thursday

sports.title: MotoGP Valencia GP: Marco Bezzecchi leads Marc Marquez in cold FP1
sports.description: Motorsport photo Marco Bezzecchi set the pace in the opening practice for the Valencia Grand Prix, leading the soon-to-be-retiring Marc Marquez. Just before the track action began on a cold but sunny Circuit Ricardo Tormo, Marquez announced his shock decision to retire from MotoGP at the end of the weekend, sending shockwaves down the paddock. sports.title: Shaquille O’Neal thinks Anthony Edwards can ruin Timberwolves if he fails to notice one thing
sports.description: Credit: Marcin Golba/NurPhoto/David Berding via Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves have been doing quite well even without Anthony Edwards, and Shaquille O’Neal has sent the superstar a warning about his eventual return. Anthony Edwards has been out indefinitely since he had arthroscopic surgery on his right knee late in October. The Minnesota Timberwolves superstar has missed the entirety of November, and will likely miss all of December and a fair amount of time in January as well. The Timberwolves haven’t struggled all that much in his absence, either. LaMelo Ball has fit the team like a glove, and they have a 14-5 record going into Friday’s game against the Memphis Grizzlies. With that in mind, Shaquille O’Neal recently shared some advice for the young superstar for when he does return. Shaquille O’Neal says Anthony Edwards will have to ensure he doesn’t disrupt team rhythm after returning The Timberwolves have played excellent team ball in Edwards’ absence. He was averaging over 33 points per game in his four games this season. Since he’s been out, though, the team has five players averaging between 12 points to 19 points per game. No one star has been dominating, and this style has been working quite well. So Shaq thinks Edwards will have to be careful with that when he does come back. “I think it’s going to be up to Anthony Edwards,” O’Neal said. “Because right now, he has to see how the guys are playing. Because they’re only playing like this because they’re eating. See, a lot of time when he has the ball, they’re just sitting in the corner, and they’re really out of rhythm. “Now that he’s not there, LaMelo’s kicking it to a damn rhythm. So he has to see this. So when he gets back, he’s going to have to get his and keep his guys in rhythm.” The likes of Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu, and Jonathan Kuminga are beginning to truly establish themselves within the context of the team. If Edwards can come back and figure out a seamless fit, no team will want to face off against the Timberwolves in the playoffs this season. sports.title: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling
sports.description: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling Joshua Kimmich made headlines earlier this week after publicly criticising the Bayern Munich hierarchy over their comments on Jamal Musiala's neurological condition and the possibility of adjusting his salary. His comments subsequently sparked speculation over whether he could face disciplinary action, potentially in the form of a fine. However, Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund has now made it clear that no such punishment is being considered. “We never discussed that, and imposing a fine was never a topic of conversation. We're really looking forward and focusing on the upcoming games,” Freund said at Friday's press conference. Sitting alongside Freund, head coach Vincent Kompany was also asked about the vice-captain's outspoken comments but declined to elaborate. Instead, he emphasised that internal matters should remain behind closed doors. “I understand what this question is getting at. However, I can't help you any further with these matters at the moment. We have our bubble, and that's how it will stay," Kompany said. “That doesn't mean we simply applaud everything internally. We tell each other the truth and openly address what hasn't gone well. But I protect these matters, and I lead by example in that regard. “If I were to comment on other issues now, I wouldn't be living up to that standard. My priority is the game against Hamburg.”

The situation is particularly troubling for the football department, where Hansi Flick’s first team has repeatedly been forced to manage injuries during demanding stretches of the season. Unfortunately, however, the concern is not limited to the senior squad, with the reserve team also experiencing a difficult run. A packed calendar is testing Barcelona’s prevention work Hansi Flick strengthened the first-team physical preparation staff in July by bringing in Benjamin Kugel , aiming to improve conditioning and reduce late-season injury problems. Hansi Flick has been dealing with player shortages, especially in defence, this season. Specifically, the stretch involving Betis, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid illustrated the cost. Eric García, Jules Kounde, Xavi Espart and Dani Olmo suffered injuries during that period, while Gerard Martin also experienced discomfort . The sequence left Flick managing absences during a demanding run of fixtures. Barça Atlètic faces the most severe shortage The reserve team has been hit especially hard. Before facing Girona B, Juliano Belletti was dealing with a shortage caused by injuries and international call-ups, with reports counting more than 20 unavailable players. Barcelona requested that the fixture be postponed, but it went ahead. Barcelona have suffered several injuries this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The match brought further damage, as Dani Avila and Ibrahim Diarra were injured , while other players finished with physical problems. Barça Atlètic subsequently lost Mirza Catovic in the derby against Espanyol B. Barcelona confirmed that Catovic had suffered a fibula fracture and would be out for around four months, taking the reserve side’s injury list to 12. Unfortunately, Barcelona’s women’s side is also dealing with a difficult injury situation, while the basketball team has been managing absences during a packed domestic and EuroLeague schedule. The pattern across several departments makes the issue bigger than an isolated run of bad luck. Barcelona have invested in prevention and recovery, but workload, travel and limited rest continue to challenge those measures.

sports.title: Ex-Patriots quarterback Joe Milton steals the show on Thanksgiving
sports.description: With one former New England Patriots quarterback in the broadcast booth, another played the game of his life. Joe Milton, under the watchful eye of Tom Brady, led the Philadelphia Eagles to a 39-38 road victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. And even on a day that saw the likes of Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Caleb Williams, Jared Goff and Dak Prescott all line up under center, it was the third-year QB that stole the show. Milton completed 21 of 31 pass attempts for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also led the game-winning drive when he marched Philadelphia’s offense into kicker Jake Elliott’s field goal range in the late fourth quarter, helping the Eagles overcome what was a 21-point deficit in the late third quarter. In addition, he proved why his “Bazooka Joe” nickname was well earned: he threw some truly spectacular passes. Every time Joe Milton made the craziest throw of the year vs the Cowboys 5 different times. pic.twitter.com/lVuL46DCmH — Cam (@42Cyc) November 27, 2026 Milton completed six of his 11 deep pass attempts versus the Cowboys, gaining 188 yards and scoring three touchdowns. He finished the game with 0.308 expected points added per play, a completion percentage 12.1 points over expectation, and an average of 17.3 air yards — ranking first among all six of the quarterbacks taking the field on Thursday. Whether he can build on the successful outing in front of a national audience will be seen. For Milton, however, it was a high point on what had been a rollercoaster of a career so far. That rollercoaster, of course, that started when the Patriots selected him in the sixth round of the 2024 draft. Milton was brought in in the same draft class as third overall pick Drake Maye, whose status as the Patriots’ future face of the franchise was never questioned. This, in turn, put his fellow then-rookie on a path to backup duty; but with veteran Jacoby Brissett also under contract at the time, not even that materialized. He ended up playing just one game as a rookie, the season finale against Buffalo a mere hours before head coach Jerod Mayo was fired. Milton completed 22 of 29 passes in that contest for 241 yards and a touchdown, leading New England to its fourth game of the year (and to drop out of the first overall draft pick). With a new regime under Mike Vrabel coming in, however, his days were numbered. In April of 2025, Milton and a seventh-round pick were sent to Dallas for a fifth-rounder. Through a series of follow-up trade, Patriots turned that selection into kicker Andy Borregales, long snapper Julian Ashby and cornerback Kobee Minor. Milton, meanwhile, played four games in his first season as a Cowboy but lost the QB2 competition this summer. technology.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
technology.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. technology.title: British social security system techies yank services offline following 'cyber incident'
technology.description: The UK's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has taken some services offline after detecting a "cyber incident," but says regular benefit and pension payments are unaffected. The department announced the precautionary shutdown on Friday morning. "We have taken some DWP online services offline as a precaution after we identified a cyber incident affecting our systems," it said. "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre (GC3) to investigate and to bring services back online as quickly as possible and to minimize any disruption. "Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal. If an online service you need is unavailable, please try again later. As always, we will never message you to ask for bank details or ask you to click on links." The Register contacted both the DWP and NCSC for more information. The DWP declined to comment beyond the statement issued publicly. GC3 coordinates responses to incidents affecting government. The Government Cyber Unit leads the wider Government Cyber Action Plan, backed by more than £210 million. It is led by the government CISO, Bella Powell. Officials have not commented on any of the usual details one would expect from a cyber incident disclosure, including the specific services that were downed, when they are expected to return, or whether any data is thought to be compromised, even at this early stage. The UK government has also been criticized recently for investing heavily in AI cyber defenses, while the issue of legacy and aging IT continues to be neglected in the background. It announced at the end of October that it was throwing £130 million at AI cyber defense technology , as part of a wider £600 million cross-government AI spending spree announced by the Treasury. technology.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
technology.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. technology.description: The end of the working week is often enough to drive tech support people to drink, which is why The Register likes to get the party started early. Friday mornings bring a new installment of On Call – the column in which we share your stories of doing whatever it takes to keep tech running. "We used to have about 30 PCs, all running slightly different radio shows depending on the time zone where we broadcast," he explained. The PCs were old clunkers running Windows 95 long after Microsoft ended support for the OS. Management knew the machines needed replacing, but funding was probably another year away. "We had to coax them on till then," Bruce wrote. "And by coax, I mean we were buying RAM on eBay because nobody sold the 4MB sticks we needed anymore." Thanks to the tender ministrations of Bruce and his colleagues, the PCs kept humming and the radio stations stayed on the air. Until a lovely spring Tuesday, when Bruce and his crew enjoyed a bucolic cup of tea in the first real sunshine of the season and received a call informing them that one of the stations was down.
